summary.text: Deb Andraca is a Democratic member of the Wisconsin State Assembly from District 23, first elected in 2020, and is seeking re-election on November 3, 2026 against Republican Aleaner Pabonnie.
A former elementary school teacher and communications professional, she sits on the Joint Finance Committee.

paragraphs.text: Deb Andraca was born in Springfield, Massachusetts, and earned a bachelor's degree from Syracuse University in 1992 and a master's degree from George Washington University in 1996.

Her career experience includes working as a vice president at FleishmanHillard International Communications, a communications director and lobbyist with the Environmental Law and Policy Center of the Midwest, and a press secretary on a congressional campaign.

In a Ballotpedia survey, she said she completed teaching coursework at Alverno College in 2018, taught third-grade math at Bruce Guadalupe Community School and served as a PTO president, Girl Scout troop leader and Milwaukee-area leader for Moms Demand Action for Gun Sense.
She said her family has lived in Whitefish Bay for more than 20 years.
Andraca defeated incumbent Republican Jim Ott in the November 3, 2020 general election for Assembly District 23 and took office on January 4, 2021.
She won re-election in 2022 against Purnima Nath and in 2024 against Laurie O'Brien Wolf.
For 2025-2026 she is assigned to the Finance Committee, the Forestry, Parks, and Outdoor Recreation Committee and the Joint Finance Committee.
In the 2026 survey she listed her campaign messages as "Safer," "Smarter" and "Healthier," and named education, gun safety reform and clean energy and conservation among her policy interests.
